mainTopic: The judges of חליצה: where each opinion learns its rules from the פסוקים, why the הלכה is three judges, and practical details of the court
overview: The גמרא finishes its proof that רבי יהודה lets ordinary people judge a חליצה. Then, with the repeated question ״ואידך״, it shows how each side uses the words ״לעיני״, ״בישראל״ (written twice) and ״ונקרא״. These words teach that the judges must see the spit, that the judges must be born Jews and not גרים, and that everyone present calls out ״חלוץ הנעל״. The גמרא asks why the plural verbs ״וקראו״ and ״ודברו״ do not add more judges. It answers that they teach that the judges call the man themselves and give him honest advice. רב נחמן rules that חליצה needs three judges. After a long back-and-forth about unnamed משניות and מיאון, the גמרא proves from a משנה in סנהדרין that רבי יהודה took back his view that five are needed. רבא adds that the court needs a fixed place, and stories show that some courts used five only to make the חליצה public. A convert, רב שמואל בר יהודה, honestly refuses to sit on such a court, and רב יהודה praises his trustworthiness. The amud ends as a new statement of רבא begins.

steps.title: A proof verse that a court must be free of blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends its argument with a פסוק showing that a regular court must be free of any blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "You are entirely beautiful, my love, and there is no blemish in you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to finish its argument that a real court cannot include anyone with a blemish, such as a blind person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חליצה needed expert judges, there would be no need to exclude blind people, because they are already unfit for a regular court. So when רבי יהודה excludes the blind, it shows that ordinary people (הדיוטות) are allowed to judge a חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: You are entirely beautiful, my love

phrases.english: As it is stated: "You are entirely beautiful, my love,
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 4:7

phrases.english: and there is no blemish in you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the argument from the previous section that רבי יהודה allows הדיוטות.
steps.raayaObject: A regular court must be free of blemishes, so excluding the blind only makes sense if הדיוטות may judge חליצה.

steps.title: How does the other opinion use the word "before the eyes"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the תנא קמא learns from ״לעיני״, since he does not use it to exclude blind people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one: what does he do with the word "before the eyes"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the תנא קמא learns from the word ״לעיני״, which רבי יהודה used to exclude blind judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that every word in the תורה teaches something. If the תנא קמא does not learn the blind exclusion from ״לעיני״, the word must be teaching him something else.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other side of the dispute)
What does he do with it? (what does he learn from it)

steps.confusionAlert: ״ואידך״ switches back and forth in this section. Here it means the תנא קמא. In the next question it means רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And the other one: that word "before the eyes of"
phrases.notes: "The other one" here is the תנא קמא, who disagrees with רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: הַהוּא לְעֵינֵי מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי יהודה's source to the other opinion's use of the same word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the תנא קמא learns from ״לעיני״.

steps.title: "Before the eyes" teaches רבא's rule about seeing the spit
steps.stepSummary: ״לעיני״ teaches רבא's rule that the judges must actually see the spit leave the יבמה's mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word comes to teach רבא's rule. רבא said: the judges must see the spit coming out of the יבמה's mouth, as it says: "before the eyes of the elders... and she shall spit."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא uses ״לעיני״ for רבא's rule: the דיינים must see the spitting with their own eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לעיני הזקנים״ is placed in the same פסוק as the spitting. So it teaches that the judges must watch the spit itself, not just know that it happened.

keyTerms.meaning: The widow who needs יבום or חליצה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule of חליצה: the judges have to see the spitting with their own eyes.

phrases.english: That word comes for the teaching of רבא.
As רבא said:
The judges need to see
the spit that comes out
from the mouth of the יבמה,
as it is written: "before the eyes of the elders... and she shall spit."
phrases.notes: דברים 25:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא uses ״לעיני״ for רבא's rule that the judges must see the spit.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה should also need it for רבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that רבי יהודה should also need ״לעיני״ for רבא's rule, so he cannot use it to exclude the blind.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the other one also needs it for רבא's teaching!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: רבא's rule is true for everyone, so רבי יהודה also needs ״לעיני״ for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״לעיני״ is used up on רבא's rule, it seems רבי יהודה has lost his source. The challenge is aimed at how רבי יהודה reads the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: This time "the other one" is רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: needs it for the teaching of רבא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 3 into a challenge against רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's rule applies to everyone, so רבי יהודה must also use ״לעיני״ for it.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns that ordinary people may judge from "in Israel"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that רבי יהודה uses ״לעיני״ for רבא's rule. He learns that הדיוטות are fine from ״בישראל״: any Jew at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. Then where does he learn that ordinary people are allowed? From "in Israel": any Jew at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and gives רבי יהודה a different source for allowing הדיוטות, the word ״בישראל״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that ordinary people may judge now comes from ״בישראל״, which says any Jew can do it. So ״לעיני״ is free for רבא's rule, and רבי יהודה's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary people who are not expert judges
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: Yes, that is so,
but then, ordinary people, from where does he learn it?
It comes from "in Israel":
phrases.notes: דברים 25:10

phrases.english: any Jew at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי וְאֶלָּא הֶדְיוֹטוֹת מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the challenge and moves the teaching to a different word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה needed ״לעיני״ as his source for allowing הדיוטות.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה uses ״לעיני״ for רבא's rule and learns that הדיוטות are allowed from ״בישראל״.

steps.title: How does the other opinion use "in Israel"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the תנא קמא learns from ״בישראל״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one: what does he do with this word "Israel"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same kind of question about the תנא קמא: if he does not use ״בישראל״ to allow ordinary people, what does it teach him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ״בישראל״ is now רבי יהודה's source, the תנא קמא must use the word for a different lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: In Israel (from the פסוק about חליצה)

phrases.english: And the other one, this word "Israel"
phrases.notes: Back to the תנא קמא now.

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ הַאי יִשְׂרָאֵל מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the other side's use of the word brought in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the תנא קמא learns from ״בישראל״.

steps.title: "In Israel" means a court of born Jews, not converts
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא uses ״בישראל״ for רב שמואל בר יהודה's teaching: the court must be made of born Jews, not גרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what רב שמואל בר יהודה taught: "in Israel" means in a court of born Jews, not in a court of converts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא learns from ״בישראל״ that the judges of חליצה must be born Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״בישראל״ is read as "born Israelites", which leaves out גרים. So the תנא קמא does not have this word free to teach that ordinary people may judge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical rule: גרים cannot sit as the judges for a חליצה.

phrases.english: He needs it for what was taught by
רב שמואל בר יהודה:
"In Israel" means in a court of Israelites,
and not in a court of converts.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנֵי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא learns from ״בישראל״ that the court must be born Jews, not גרים.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה learn the rule about converts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה learns the rule excluding גרים, since he used ״בישראל״ to allow ordinary people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: In just one word, the גמרא asks how רבי יהודה knows that גרים cannot judge, since his ״בישראל״ is already used up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה surely agrees that a court of גרים is not valid. But his ״בישראל״ went to allowing הדיוטות, so he needs another source.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Now it is רבי יהודה: where does he learn that גרים can't judge?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for רבי יהודה's source for the rule given in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהודה's source for excluding גרים.

steps.title: Another "in Israel" is written
steps.stepSummary: The word ״בישראל״ appears a second time, and רבי יהודה learns the rule about גרים from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another "in Israel" is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוקים of חליצה say ״בישראל״ twice, so רבי יהודה uses the second one for the rule about converts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two separate words, רבי יהודה can learn two separate rules: ordinary people may judge, and גרים may not.

phrases.english: Another "in Israel" is written.
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7 and 25:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה learns the rule about גרים from the second ״בישראל״.

steps.title: How does the other opinion use the second "in Israel"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the תנא קמא learns from the second ״בישראל״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the תנא קמא does with the second ״בישראל״, since he used only one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא used one ״בישראל״ for the rule about גרים. The second one must teach him something else.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Back to the תנא קמא: what does he do with the second "in Israel"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the other side's use of the extra word from step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the תנא קמא learns from the second ״בישראל״.

steps.title: Everyone present calls out "the one whose shoe was removed"
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא uses the second ״בישראל״ for a ברייתא: רבי טרפון told everyone present at a חליצה to call out ״חלוץ הנעל״.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא. רבי יהודה said: Once we were sitting before רבי טרפון, and a יבמה came to do חליצה. He said to us: All of you, call out "the one whose shoe was removed."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא uses the second ״בישראל״ for רבי טרפון's practice that all the people present call out ״חלוץ הנעל״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״ונקרא שמו בישראל״ is read as saying that the whole crowd of Jews present calls out the name ״חלוץ הנעל״. So the תנא קמא's extra word is used for this practice.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
The one whose shoe was removed

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the custom that everyone at a חליצה calls out ״חלוץ הנעל״.

phrases.english: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא:
רבי יהודה said:
Once we were sitting
before רבי טרפון,
and a יבמה came to do חליצה,
and he said to us,
"All of you, call out: 'The one whose shoe was removed.'"
phrases.notes: These words come from דברים 25:10. Everyone says them after the חליצה is done.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא uses the second ״בישראל״ to teach that everyone present calls out ״חלוץ הנעל״.

steps.title: Where רבי יהודה learns that everyone calls out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה used the second ״בישראל״ for the rule about גרים, so the גמרא asks where he learns רבי טרפון's rule. It answers that he learns it from the word ״וְנִקְרָא״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי יהודה, where does he learn it from? He learns it from the word ״וְנִקְרָא״ ("and it shall be called").
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick question and answers it right away. Since רבי יהודה already used both times ״בישראל״ appears, where does he get the rule that everyone at the חליצה calls out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11 the תנא קמא learned the calling-out rule from the second ״בישראל״. רבי יהודה needs that ״בישראל״ for the rule about גרים, so he needs a different source. The גמרא says he learns it from ״וְנִקְרָא״: the word 'called' itself tells us that people call out.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the other opinion. Here it is רבי יהודה.
"And it shall be called", the word from the פסוק of חליצה
It comes out from, meaning he learns it from

phrases.english: And the other?
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה again: where does he learn that everyone present calls out?

phrases.english: He derives it from "and it shall be called."
phrases.notes: דברים 25:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds a source for רבי יהודה for the rule the תנא קמא learned from the second ״בישראל״ in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where רבי יהודה learns that everyone present at the חליצה calls out.
steps.whatToRemember: Each side uses every word: ״לעיני״ teaches that the judges must see the spit. One ״בישראל״ teaches either that any Jew may judge (רבי יהודה) or that גרים may not (תנא קמא). The second ״בישראל״ teaches the other side's rule: for רבי יהודה, the rule about גרים; for the תנא קמא, that everyone calls out ״חלוץ הנעל״. רבי יהודה learns the calling-out rule from ״ונקרא״.

steps.title: Other plural words should add even more judges
steps.stepSummary: If the plural word for 'elders' adds judges, then the plural verbs ״וְקָרְאוּ״ and ״וְדִבְּרוּ״ should each add two more. That would mean nine judges for רבי יהודה and seven for the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, ״וְקָרְאוּ״ ("and they shall call") means two more, and ״וְדִבְּרוּ״ ("and they shall speak") means two more! Then for רבי יהודה there should be nine judges, and for the רבנן seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the argument about how many judges a חליצה needs. It challenges the method of counting judges from plural words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, both opinions counted judges from the plural word for 'elders': the רבנן reached three and רבי יהודה reached five. The challenge is that the פסוק has two more plural verbs, ״וְקָרְאוּ״ and ״וְדִבְּרוּ״. Each should add two judges, giving seven for the רבנן and nine for רבי יהודה, and nobody holds that.

keyTerms.meaning: But now that you say so. This opens a challenge that pushes your logic further.
So too, meaning following the same logic

phrases.english: But if that is so,
"and they shall call" — two,
phrases.notes: דברים 25:8. A plural verb means at least two people.

phrases.english: "and they shall speak" — two!
So too, according to רבי יהודה
there are nine here,
phrases.notes: His five judges plus four more.

phrases.english: according to the Rabbis there are seven here!
phrases.notes: Their three judges plus four more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question about calling out and returns to counting judges from the plural words of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The method both opinions use: counting judges from plural words in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If plural words add judges, then the two plural verbs in the same פסוק should add four more judges. That would give seven or nine judges, which no one holds.

steps.title: Those words teach other lessons
steps.stepSummary: ״וְקָרְאוּ״ and ״וְדִבְּרוּ״ are needed for a ברייתא, so they do not add judges. ״וְקָרְאוּ לוֹ״ teaches that the judges themselves must call him, not messengers. ״וְדִבְּרוּ אֵלָיו״ teaches that they give him good advice, for example not to marry someone whose age is far from his.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: "They shall call him" means the judges themselves, not their messengers. "They shall speak to him" teaches that they give him advice that fits him. If he was young and she was old, or he was old and she was young, they tell him: What are you doing with a young girl? What are you doing with an old woman? Go to someone like you, and do not bring fighting into your home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. These two verbs are already used for other lessons, so they cannot also be used to add judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word in the תורה that already teaches one lesson is not used to count judges. ״וְקָרְאוּ לוֹ״ teaches that the judges must do the calling themselves. ״וְדִבְּרוּ אֵלָיו״ teaches that the court gives the man honest advice, such as not to do יבום with a woman much older or much younger than he is, so that there will be no fighting at home.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for him, meaning this word is used for a different lesson
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Advice that fits him, good and proper advice

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the court in a חליצה case does more than run a ceremony. It is supposed to guide the man toward what is good for his home.

phrases.english: That is needed for him
for that which is taught in a ברייתא:
"They shall call him" — and not their messengers,
"and they shall speak to him" —
teaches that they give him
advice that is right for him.
For if he was young
and she was old,
or he was old and she was young,
they say to him:
What are you doing with a young girl?
What are you doing with an old woman?
Go to someone like you,
phrases.notes: Literally 'go toward one who is like you,' meaning someone close to your age.

phrases.english: and do not bring a quarrel
into your home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 by showing that the two verbs are already used for other lessons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The words are needed for another lesson, so they are not free to add judges.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every plural word in the פסוק adds two more judges.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְקָרְאוּ״ teaches that the judges themselves call him, and ״וְדִבְּרוּ״ teaches that they give him fitting advice. Neither adds judges.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules that חליצה needs three judges
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב נחמן: the הלכה is that חליצה is done before three judges, because the unnamed משנה at the start of the פרק says so.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: The הלכה is that חליצה is done before three, since the תנא taught us an unnamed משנה that follows this view.
steps.whatsHappening: After the back-and-forth over the פסוקים, the גמרא gives a practical ruling: the הלכה follows the רבנן, so three judges are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that when a משנה states a law without a name (סתם משנה), the הלכה follows it. The משנה at the start of the פרק says without a name that חליצה is done before three, so רב נחמן rules that way and not like רבי יהודה's five.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא taught us without a name, meaning an unnamed משנה

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, חליצה is done before three judges, like the רבנן, because the unnamed משנה says so.

phrases.english: רבא said that רב נחמן said:
The halakha is that חליצה is before three,
since the tanna taught us an unnamed ruling like it.
phrases.notes: This is the unnamed משנה at the beginning of this פרק, which says חליצה is done before three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where each opinion learns its number to which opinion is the practical הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is that חליצה is done before three, following the unnamed משנה.

steps.title: רבא: then מיאון should also need three
steps.stepSummary: רבא pushes back on רב נחמן: if we follow the unnamed משנה, then מיאון should also need three, since a משנה lists מיאון together with חליצה as needing three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: If so, then מיאון also needs three, as we learned in a משנה: מיאון and חליצה are done before three.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן's reasoning. This sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's reason was 'follow the unnamed משנה.' But another unnamed משנה puts מיאון right next to חליצה and says both need three. So, by the same reason, רב נחמן should also rule that מיאון needs three.

keyTerms.meaning: Refusal: a girl who was married off as a minor by her mother or brother can refuse the marriage and end it

phrases.english: רבא said to רב נחמן:
If so, refusal too,
phrases.notes: He means: by your reasoning, you should also rule that מיאון needs three judges.

phrases.english: as we learned: Refusal and חליצה are before three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב נחמן's reason from Step 15 and applies it to מיאון, which the same משנה lists next to חליצה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reason for ruling that חליצה needs three: following the unnamed משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same unnamed משנה says מיאון also needs three, so by the same reasoning רב נחמן must rule that way for מיאון too.

steps.title: Proof that רב נחמן does not require three for מיאון
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say that מיאון really does need three. The גמרא blocks this with a ברייתא and a ruling of רב נחמן that follows the opinion allowing two.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that מיאון really does need three, that cannot be. A ברייתא teaches: about מיאון, בית שמאי say it needs a court of experts. בית הלל say it can be done in such a court or not in such a court. Both agree that three people are needed. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי say two are enough. And רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: the הלכה follows that pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's challenge from Step 16. It shows that רב נחמן himself ruled that מיאון can be done before two people, so he did not follow the unnamed משנה there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's reason for requiring three in חליצה was 'follow the unnamed משנה.' Yet for מיאון he ruled like the pair of תנאים who allow two, against an unnamed משנה that requires three. So his reasoning looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: the גמרא blocks a possible answer before anyone gives it.
A girl married off as a minor refuses the marriage, which ends it.
They say it is valid with only two people.
The pair, meaning the two תנאים named together.

steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל's 'not in a court' does not mean fewer than three people. It means three ordinary people who are not expert judges. Both בית שמאי and בית הלל still require three.

phrases.english: And if you would say: indeed so,
phrases.notes: He means: maybe מיאון really does need three judges.

phrases.english: but isn't it taught in a ברייתא: regarding refusal,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים בֵּית דִּין מוּמְחִין,
phrases.english: בית שמאי say: a court of experts,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: בְּבֵית דִּין וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין.
phrases.english: and בית הלל say: in a court or not in a court.
Both agree that three are needed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי
say it is valid with two.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: And רב יוסף בר מניומי said that רב נחמן said:
The הלכה follows that pair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of Step 16 by showing what רב נחמן actually ruled about מיאון.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reason in Step 15, that we follow the unnamed משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן ruled like the pair who allow two for מיאון, against an unnamed משנה. So 'follow the unnamed משנה' cannot be his whole reason for חליצה.

steps.title: מיאון has one unnamed משנה, חליצה has two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that חליצה is supported by two unnamed משניות, while מיאון has only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, for מיאון, there is only one unnamed משנה. Here, for חליצה, there are two unnamed משניות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by counting the unnamed משניות on each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that one unnamed משנה is not strong enough to settle the הלכה, but two are. So רב נחמן could rule against the single one about מיאון and still follow the two about חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed משנה, a ruling stated with no name attached.

phrases.english: There there is one unnamed ruling,
phrases.notes: 'There' is מיאון. The one unnamed משנה is in סנהדרין, which lists the cases that need three.

phrases.english: and here there are two unnamed rulings.
phrases.notes: For חליצה: our משנה here, plus that same משנה in סנהדרין.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם חַד סְתָמָא, וְהָכָא תְּרֵי סְתָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 16-17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction by the number of unnamed משניות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases have equal unnamed support, so רב נחמן is inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: חליצה has two unnamed משניות and מיאון has only one, so they are not equal.

steps.title: מיאון also has two unnamed משניות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: מיאון also has a second unnamed משנה, which says a judge may marry a woman who did מיאון before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, for מיאון, there are two unnamed משניות. As we learned: if she did מיאון or חליצה in front of him, he may marry her, because he was sitting as a court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 18 by finding a second unnamed משנה about מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the man counts as a court when she does מיאון in front of him. That implies מיאון is done in a court of three. So מיאון also has two unnamed sources, and the count in Step 18 falls apart.

phrases.english: There too there are two unnamed rulings,
as we learned in a משנה: if she refused or did חליצה in front of him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is a man who sat as one of the judges. This משנה is earlier in יבמות (25b).

phrases.english: he may marry her, because he is part of a court.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי תְּרֵי סְתָמֵי נִינְהוּ, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the counting answer of Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מיאון has only one unnamed משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second unnamed משנה treats מיאון as done before a court, so מיאון also has two unnamed sources.

steps.title: Revised count: two for מיאון, three for חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that מיאון has two unnamed משניות but says חליצה has three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there, for מיאון, there are two unnamed משניות. Here, for חליצה, there are three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the point of Step 19 and recounts. חליצה still comes out ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same משנה that gave מיאון a second source also mentions חליצה. So חליצה gains a third source, and it still has more unnamed support than מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: dropping the earlier answer and giving a new one.

phrases.english: Rather, there there are two unnamed rulings,
here there are three unnamed rulings.
phrases.notes: The משנה just quoted mentions חליצה too, so חליצה now has three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָתָם תְּרֵי סְתָמֵי הָכָא תְּלָתָא סְתָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Revises the answer of Step 18 after the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A revised count of unnamed משניות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Now both cases have two, so they seem equal.
steps.terutzMaskana: חליצה has three and מיאון has two, so חליצה still has more support.

steps.title: Why should the number of unnamed משניות matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the counting approach: an unnamed משנה is an unnamed משנה, whether there is one, two, or three.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, this is an unnamed משנה and that is an unnamed משנה. What difference does it make whether there is one, two, or three?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the whole idea of counting. It says the number of unnamed משניות should not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה' depends on the kind of source, not on how many there are. Once each side has an unnamed משנה, adding more does not give one side more weight. So the answers in Steps 18 and 20 fail.

keyTerms.meaning: After all, consider: introduces a point both sides already accept.
What difference does it make to me?

phrases.english: After all, this is unnamed and that is unnamed,
what difference is it to me if there is one unnamed ruling,
what difference is it to me if there are two unnamed rulings,
what difference is it to me if there are three?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counting idea behind Steps 18 and 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that more unnamed משניות give a ruling more force.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unnamed משנה gets its force from being unnamed, not from being repeated. So both cases stand equal, and the question on רב נחמן comes back.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins a new answer
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק starts a new answer: the unnamed משנה about חליצה was placed right where there is an argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: since the unnamed ruling was placed where there is an argument,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the counting approach, and רב נחמן בר יצחק begins a new explanation. This is only the opening of his sentence, and it continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new answer looks at where the unnamed משנה appears, not how many there are. The unnamed ruling that חליצה needs three sits right next to an argument about how many judges are needed. רבי יהודה says five there. The rest of his reasoning comes in Steps 23 and 24.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed ruling placed right where there is an argument.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here thinking the answer is done. The sentence is cut off, and the actual conclusion comes in the next line of the גמרא.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
since the unnamed ruling is placed where there is an argument,
phrases.notes: The argument is in the same משנה: רבי יהודה says five judges for other cases there. The sentence goes on in the next line.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הוֹאִיל וּסְתָם בִּמְקוֹם מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected counting approach with a new reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new explanation based on where the unnamed ruling is placed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Counting the unnamed משניות explains the difference, and that has just been rejected.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer is still being stated. It rests on the unnamed ruling sitting right next to an argument.

steps.title: The משנה where the unnamed rule about חליצה sits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in סנהדרין. רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה argue about סמיכת זקנים and עגלה ערופה, and right after that the משנה says without any name: חליצה and מיאון need three.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: סמיכת זקנים and עגלה ערופה need three judges, says רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says five. חליצה and מיאון need three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual משנה that רב נחמן בר יצחק was talking about. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will draw a lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unnamed line about חליצה comes right after a case where רבי יהודה argues. That placement is the point: if רבי יהודה still disagreed about חליצה, the משנה would have recorded his argument here too.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown

phrases.english: As we learned: ordination of elders and the calf whose neck is broken
phrases.notes: This משנה is in סנהדרין 2a.

phrases.english: are done before three; these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says: before five.
Ḥalitza and refusals are done before three,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the משנה that רב נחמן בר יצחק referred to in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That the unnamed rule about חליצה was placed right where רבי יהודה argues

steps.title: רבי יהודה changed his mind about חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה argued about the first cases but stayed silent about חליצה. So he must have changed his mind, and the גמרא agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה does not argue here. Learn from this that רבי יהודה changed his mind. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the silence of רבי יהודה in the משנה as proof that he gave up his view that חליצה needs five, and it accepts that proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting unnamed משניות did not work in step 21. This proof is stronger: an unnamed rule placed right next to a dispute shows that the person who argued there accepts it. That is why the law follows the unnamed משנה about חליצה: three judges are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He took back his earlier opinion
Learn from this. Said a second time, it means the גמרא agrees.

steps.whatToRemember: The law is that חליצה needs only three judges, because רבי יהודה took back his view that it needs five.
steps.confusionAlert: The first שמע מינה states the proof. The second שמע מינה, standing alone, is the גמרא saying 'yes, that is right.' They are not the same statement repeated.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda does not argue —

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ הֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: learn from this that Rabbi Yehuda took back his view.
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the משנה quoted in step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה changed his mind, so חליצה is done before three judges.

steps.title: רבא: the judges must set a fixed place
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that judges doing חליצה must set a fixed place for it, based on the פסוק 'to the gate, to the elders.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The judges need to set a fixed place, as it says, 'His יבמה shall go up to the gate, to the elders.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about how חליצה is carried out. רבא says the court must have a set location.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'gate' in the פסוק points to a known, set place where the elders sit. So the court cannot do חליצה just anywhere. It needs a place that was set in advance.

keyTerms.meaning: His יבמה, the widow who is waiting for יבום or חליצה

phrases.english: Rava said: The judges need
to set a fixed place,
as it is written: 'His yevama shall go up
to the gate, to the elders.'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: צְרִיכִי דַּיָּינֵי לְמִיקְבַּע דּוּכְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about how חליצה is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court must set a fixed place for doing חליצה.

steps.title: A חליצה done with five judges
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע did a חליצה with five judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע did a case of חליצה with five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what two אמוראים actually did. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that three judges are enough, yet these אמוראים used five. That seems to follow רבי יהודה's old view, which he gave up.

keyTerms.meaning: They did a case in practice

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
did a case with five.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עָבְדִי עוֹבָדָא בְּחַמְשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a practice that seems to go against the conclusion of step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, a חליצה was done before five judges.

steps.title: Why use five if רבי יהודה changed his mind?
steps.stepSummary: Who did they follow? רבי יהודה? But he changed his mind!
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? רבי יהודה's? But he took it back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the practice of using five judges, since the only source for five was a view that was taken back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 showed that רבי יהודה gave up his view, so nobody holds that five are needed. Why would these אמוראים follow a view that no one holds anymore?

keyTerms.meaning: But look, ... (used to raise a problem)

phrases.english: Following whom? Following Rabbi Yehuda?
But he took back his view!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְהָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice reported in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of רב פפא and רב הונא of using five judges
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Five judges only fits רבי יהודה's old view, and he took that view back.

steps.title: Five judges only to make it public
steps.stepSummary: They used five only so that the חליצה would become well known, not because it was required.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was to make the matter public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra judges were not a legal requirement. They were there to spread word of the חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law still needs only three. Adding more people makes the event better known, so everyone learns that this woman is now free to marry.
steps.whatToRemember: Three judges are what the law requires. Five is an extra step taken only to make the חליצה known.

phrases.english: To make the matter public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using five judges means they held five are required.
steps.terutzMaskana: Five were used only to make it public. Three is the requirement.

steps.title: רב כהנא invites רב אשי to be the fifth
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי visited רב כהנא, who asked him to come and fill out a group of five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי came to רב כהנא's house. רב כהנא said to him: Will the master come up with us to fill out the five?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the custom of using five judges for חליצה. This sets up רב כהנא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even great אמוראים like רב כהנא tried to gather five people for a חליצה. This shows the custom was well established.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi happened to come to Rav Kahana's house,
he said to him: Will the master come up with us
to fill out the group of five?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing the custom explained in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The custom was to gather five people for a חליצה.

steps.title: רב כהנא's memory of רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא recalls that רב יהודה once asked him to come up to the bundle of reeds to join the five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I was standing before רב יהודה, and he said to me: Come up to the bundle of reeds to join the five.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא explains where his custom comes from: his teacher רב יהודה did the same. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'bundle of reeds' was the set place where רב יהודה's court did חליצה, which matches רבא's rule in step 25. The number five here matches what רב פפא and רב הונא did.

keyTerms.meaning: To join, to be counted together with

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: I was standing before Rav Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לִי: תָּא סַק לְזִירְזָא דִּקְנֵי,
phrases.english: and he said to me: Come, go up to the bundle of reeds,
phrases.notes: The bundle of reeds marked the court's set spot for חליצה, like רבא required.

phrases.english: to join the group of five.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב כהנא gives the source of his own custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה gathered five at a set place for חליצה.

steps.title: Why do we need five?
steps.stepSummary: The people there asked רב יהודה why five were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Why do I need five?
steps.whatsHappening: The people present ask רב יהודה the same question the גמרא asked in step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They knew that three is enough, so asking for five looked strange. This sets up רב יהודה's explanation.

phrases.english: They said to him: Why do I need five?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the request in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for having five judges when three are enough

steps.title: רב יהודה: so the matter becomes known
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answered that five were there to make the חליצה public.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: So that the matter will become known.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה himself gives the same reason the גמרא gave in step 28.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up the גמרא's answer with a story: the custom of five comes from wanting publicity, not from a legal requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: So that it will become known

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלִיפַּרְסַם מִילְּתָא.
phrases.english: He said to them: So that the matter will become known.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Five are used only to make the חליצה public.

steps.title: רב יהודה invites רב שמואל בר יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asked רב שמואל בר יהודה to come up to the bundle of reeds and join the five, to make the matter public.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יהודה was standing before רב יהודה. רב יהודה said to him: Come up to the bundle of reeds to join the five, to make the matter public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story with the same invitation. This sets up a surprising reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The invitation matches the earlier story word for word. What is new here is the reply of the person who was invited.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda was standing before Rav Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סַק תָּא לְזִירְזָא דִּקְנֵי
phrases.english: he said to him: Go up, come to the bundle of reeds
to join the group of five, to make the matter public.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about inviting someone to be one of the five.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה invited another person to be one of the five, to make the חליצה public.

steps.title: A convert may not sit on a חליצה court
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה declined. He quoted a ברייתא that 'in ישראל' means a court of born Jews, not of converts, and he was a convert.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned that 'in ישראל' means a court of born Jews, not a court of converts, and I am a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The invited person turns down the seat on the court. He explains that as a convert he cannot be a judge for חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in ישראל' in the פסוק about חליצה teach that the judges must be born Jews. So a convert cannot be counted on a חליצה court, not even as one of the extra judges added for publicity.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In ישראל', words from the פסוק about חליצה

steps.whatToRemember: A חליצה court must be made of born Jews. A גר cannot serve on it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a qualification for the judges of חליצה that goes beyond simply having the right number of judges.

phrases.english: He said to him: We learned: 'In Israel' —
phrases.notes: From דברים 25:10, 'and his name shall be called in Israel.'

phrases.english: means in a court of born Israelites
and not in a court of converts,
and I am a convert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns down the invitation from step 33.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only his own place on the court, not the custom of using five
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A convert is not fit to judge חליצה, because the פסוק requires a court of born Jews.

steps.title: רב יהודה would trust רב שמואל בר יהודה even with money
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that for someone as honest as רב שמואל בר יהודה, he would take money from a person based on his word alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Someone like רב שמואל בר יהודה, I would take money out of a person's hands based on what he says.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה praises רב שמואל בר יהודה, who just showed his honesty by revealing that he was a convert. He says he would trust such a man enough to take money based on his word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody knew רב שמואל בר יהודה was a convert until he said so himself. That honesty makes רב יהודה say he would trust him even in money cases. The next step will ask whether that can really be true.

keyTerms.meaning: I would take out (money from someone)
based on his word (literally, 'on his mouth')

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Someone like Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda,
phrases.notes: This is the same person who just told everyone he was a convert, back in Step 34.

phrases.english: I would take out money based on his word.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: כְּגוֹן רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רב שמואל בר יהודה's honest admission in Step 34 by praising how trustworthy he is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person as honest as רב שמואל בר יהודה could be trusted enough to take money based on his word.

steps.title: The Torah requires two witnesses to take money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב יהודה could take money on one person's word, when the תורה says a matter is set only by two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think he would take money out? But the תורה said, 'By the mouth of two witnesses'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's words. It points out that the תורה requires two witnesses, so one person, however honest, cannot cause money to be taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of two witnesses is a clear law of the תורה, not a matter of how much we trust someone. So taking money based on one witness cannot be what רב יהודה meant. This forces the גמרא to reread his statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (meaning: that can't be right)
but look, isn't it true that
by the mouth of two witnesses

phrases.english: Would it enter your mind that I would take out money?
But surely, "By the mouth of two witnesses"
phrases.notes: דברים 19:15

phrases.english: is what the Merciful One said!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the plain meaning of רב יהודה's statement in Step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that he would take money based on one person's word.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה requires two witnesses to establish a matter, so one witness can never be enough to take money, no matter how honest he is.

steps.title: He meant he would weaken a loan document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב יהודה meant he would weaken a loan document based on that honest man's word, not take money directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant: I would weaken a loan document based on his word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. רב יהודה did not mean taking money; he meant that one honest man's word could weaken a loan document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking money from someone needs two witnesses. But if a trusted person says a debt was already paid, רב יהודה would not let the lender collect with that document. That is a smaller step, so it does not break the two-witness rule.
steps.whatToRemember: One witness cannot take money from someone, but רב יהודה would trust a very honest person enough to weaken a loan document.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה is not saying one witness can take money. The גמרא's answer limits his praise to weakening a document, not collecting money.

phrases.english: Rather: I would weaken a document based on his word.
phrases.notes: If he says the loan was already paid, the document could no longer be used to collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 36 by rereading רב יהודה's statement more narrowly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the statement to mean something smaller
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה would take money based on one honest witness.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה would only weaken a loan document based on one honest witness, which does not need two witnesses.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One trusted person's word can weaken a loan document, but cannot by itself take money from someone.

steps.title: רבא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement from רבא, which continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup. It opens a statement by רבא, and his actual words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the topic of a convert sitting on a חליצה court just came up, the גמרא brings a related teaching from רבא. His actual statement continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rava said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the story about רב שמואל בר יהודה to a new statement connected to converts and the חליצה court.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling itself appears in the next section; this line only introduces רבא as the speaker.
